articles.title: Did the Earth vibrate for 9 days? How the Greenland landslide pulsed the Earth worldwide for over a week
articles.summary: A significant landslide in Greenland reportedly caused the Earth to vibrate worldwide for over a week, lasting approximately nine days. This unusual geological event demonstrates how localized incidents can generate global seismic pulses, highlighting the interconnectedness of our planet's geological systems. Such phenomena offer valuable insights into Earth's complex dynamics.

articles.title: 77 hospitalised after military plane crashes in Colombia
articles.summary: A Colombian air force plane carrying 125 individuals crashed shortly after takeoff in the country's southern Amazon region. The accident resulted in one fatality and 77 people requiring hospitalization. This incident involving a military asset occurred deep within Colombian territory, prompting an investigation into the cause. The president acknowledged the tragic event, underscoring the complexities of operations in remote areas.

articles.title: Karim Lopez NBA mock draft projection: Where the forward is expected to land
articles.summary: March Madness is underway, providing a critical platform for college basketball stars aiming for this summer's NBA draft. Notably, an international prospect, not involved in the tournament, has already captured significant attention from scouts. This illustrates the intense competition and global reach of talent seeking entry into the US's premier professional basketball league, underscoring the diverse recruitment landscape.

articles.title: India will become developed nation by 2047: ISRO chief V Narayanan
articles.summary: ISRO Chairman V Narayanan expressed confidence in Kolkata that India will achieve developed nation status by its 100th year of independence. This aligns with the 'Viksit Bharat' vision, highlighting national aspirations for progress and self-reliance. Such statements from scientific leaders underscore India's commitment to technological advancement and economic growth, crucial for future defense capabilities.

articles.title: Cycling-friendly London borough finally set to introduce dockless hire bikes – but Labour accused of “desperate ploy” to win back Green voters
articles.summary: A prominent cycling-friendly borough in London is launching an e-bike hire scheme, marking its first in nearly a decade. This move signals a potential shift away from previous dockless initiatives that faced criticism. The introduction of accessible e-bikes aims to enhance urban mobility and promote sustainable transport options within the city, reflecting evolving strategies in public hire services.

articles.title: Introducing the Venezianico Nereide Verdigris
articles.summary: Venice's enduring beauty is highlighted despite facing severe threats to its existence. These include environmental risks like sinking into the ocean and degradation from heavy tourism, pigeons, and brackish canal waters. The city's unique charm persists amidst these ongoing challenges, underscoring critical international efforts required for preserving such iconic global heritage.

articles.title: NavIC: India's "jinxed" navigational program, or a cornerstone of India's misplaced space priorities?
articles.summary: India's indigenous NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) is a crucial regional satellite navigation system. It provides accurate Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) services across India and its surrounding regions. This system enhances strategic autonomy, reduces reliance on foreign GPS, and is vital for national security and civilian applications, boosting India's self-reliance.
